name: Chamber Strings
description: A small bowed string section: a few players on every note, each with their own pitch, vibrato and bow, heard through wooden bodies with bow noise and mutes.

params.name: Players
params.description: How many instruments play each note, from one soloist to a small section. More players sound thicker and less exact, not louder.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How slowly the bows start a note. Short speaks at once; long is a swell that grows out of the bow noise.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long a note takes to die away after the key is let go.

params.name: Bow
params.description: Where the bow meets the string. Low is over the fingerboard, soft and flute-like; high is near the bridge, glassy with a thin fundamental.

params.name: Air
params.description: Bow hiss riding on the tone. Towards the top the tone itself thins to a breathy whisper.

params.name: Vibrato
params.description: How wide each player's vibrato is. Every player has their own speed and starts a little after the note; at zero the notes are still.

params.name: Mute
params.description: A mute on the bridge. It veils the top of the sound and makes it a little nasal.

params.name: Scatter
params.description: How loosely the players agree in pitch and timing: a tight unison or a ragged section. With one player it sets how far the pitch wanders.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far the players are spread between left and right. At zero everything is in the middle.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many notes stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. It models what a listener knows a small bowed section by, not the strings themselves: each note is one to six sawtooth players (the force of a bowed string on its bridge is close to a sawtooth) with their own pitch offset, drift, vibrato, entry and bow changes, through two fixed banks of body resonances and filtered bow noise. Simplified: no string or bow physics, no coupling between notes, one low and one high body shared by every note, and a mute that is an equaliser. The violin's air and body resonances near 280, 470 and 550 Hz and its bridge hill at 2 to 3 kHz are from the published acoustics; the low body's resonances, the filler resonances of both, every Q, every per-player range (pitch spread, drift, vibrato rate, depth and delay, entry stagger, bow-change timing and depth), the bow filter's multiples and the mute's curve are choices made for this device. It is not a circuit or a sample emulation.
